'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations]]
****[[Red Sea crisis]], [[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
*****[[Iran]] announces a pause on peace talks with the [[United States]], and, alongside the [[Axis of Resistance]], announces plans to "[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis|completely block]]" the [[Strait of Hormuz]] and threatens to close the [[Bab el-Mandeb Strait|Strait of Mandeb]], ruling out any further talks until [[Israel]] ends its [[military operation]]s in [[Lebanon]] and [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://aje.news/xhk3kr?update=4617169 (Al Jazeera)]

*****[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian foreign minister]] [[Abbas Araghchi]] asks [[Pakistan]]i [[Minister for Foreign Affairs (Pakistan)|foreign minister]] and [[Deputy Prime Minister of Pakistan|deputy prime minister]] [[Ishaq Dar|Mohammad Ishaq Dar]] to help facilitate [[de-escalation]] and express concern about [[Israel]]'s violations of [[2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire|the ceasefire in Lebanon]]. ****[[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] says that [[ceasefire]] negotiations are still ongoing, contradicting reports of [[Iran]] backing out of talks. [https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/5904329-trump-iran-talks-suspended/ (''The Hill'')]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign]]

***[[2026 Lebanon war]]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Iran war fuel crisis]]
***[[Oil price]]s increase by nearly 8% on the announcement of the peace talks ending, with [[West Texas Intermediate]] rising to [[United States dollar|US$]]94.20 per [[barrel (unit)|barrel]] and [[Brent Crude]] to US$97.23 per barrel. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/01/oil-prices-wti-brent-crude-israel-lebanon-hezbollah-iran-trump-us.html (CNBC)]
**Terminal 1 at [[Kuwait International Airport]] resumes operations as part of a phased reopening plan following repair, development, and upgrade works. Additionally, the airport resumes operations to Arab and foreign airlines after the airport has been closed since the war started on February 28. [https://kuwaittimes.com/article/44309/kuwait/kuwait-intl-airport-resumes-operations-for-arab-foreign-airlines/ (''Kuwait Times'')] [https://www.arabtimesonline.com/news/terminal-1-at-kuwait-airport-reopens-for-arrivals-and-departures/ (''Arab Times Kuwait'')]
*[[2026 Cuban crisis]]
**[[Canada|Canadian]] hotel operator [[Blue Diamond Resorts]] ends its operations in [[Cuba]], citing reduced air service and operational challenges after managing 62 properties on the island. [https://www.indopremier.com/ipotnews/newsDetail.php?jdl=Canadian_hotel_group_Blue_Diamond_shuts_Cuba_operations&news_id=1731761&group_news=ALLNEWS&taging_subtype=IRAN&name=&search=y_general&q=IRAN,%20&halaman=1 (AFP via Indo Premier)]

**A ban on children under the age of 16 using [[social media]] formally enters force in [[Malaysia]]. **[[Senator of the Philippines|Philippine senator]] [[Jinggoy Estrada]] and former [[Secretary of Public Works and Highways|public works secretary]] [[Manuel Bonoan]] surrender to [[Philippine National Police|police]] after an [[Sandiganbayan|anti-graft court]] orders their arrest on [[plunder]] charges related to an alleged [[Philippine peso|₱]]573-million (US$9.3-million) [[Corruption in the Philippines|corruption]] scheme involving [[flood control]] projects. *[[Murder of Henry Nowak]]
**Vickrum Digwa, a 23-year-old [[Sikhism in the United Kingdom|Sikh]] man, is sentenced to [[Life imprisonment in England and Wales|life imprisonment]], with a minimum of 21 years, for [[Murder in English law|murdering]] 18-year-old [[University of Southampton]] student Henry Nowak in [[Southampton]], [[England]], on 3 December 2025. Digwa's mother is also found guilty of [[Assisting offender|assisting an offender]] by hiding the murder weapon, a knife. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/jun/01/southampton-man-jailed-life-murder-student-religious-knife-vickrum-digwa-henry-nowak (''The Guardian'')]

*[[Regulation of artificial intelligence in the United States]]
**The [[U.S. state]] of [[Florida]] files a lawsuit against [[OpenAI]] [[chief executive officer|CEO]] [[Sam Altman]] and [[Artificial intelligence|AI]]-[[chatbot]] [[ChatGPT]], accusing the chatbot of putting profit over safety. This lawsuit is the first to be filed by a U.S. state against ChatGPT.
